introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0510 Biology 1, June 2026, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the best answer, A, B, C or D. Section I (questions 1-7): independent questions. Section II (8-20): biological diagrams. Section III (21-25): one or more of the responses 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Section IV (26-30): two statements to compare. Section V (31-40): choose the heading related to a description. Section VI (41-50): biological situations.

Outline of the human body showing numbered endocrine glands: 1 and 2 in the head, 3 at the neck, X at the pancreas, 4 and 5 in the lower abdomen (Question 14).
Body temperature of animals against external temperature: the rat is a horizontal line at about 37 degrees, the toad a rising straight line (Question 44).
Rate of photosynthesis against temperature: rises to a maximum at point X, then falls (Question 48).

questions.enonce_markdown: The point of attachment of the leaf to the stem is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: A node is the point on the stem where a leaf (and its axillary bud) is attached. The internode is the stretch of stem between two nodes, the axil is the angle between the leaf stalk and the stem, and the apex is the tip of the leaf or shoot. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The contractile vacuole in Amoeba helps in:
questions.corrige_markdown: The contractile vacuole of a freshwater Amoeba collects excess water that enters by osmosis and expels it, so the cell does not burst. This control of water content is osmoregulation. Movement uses pseudopodia, feeding uses food vacuoles and reproduction is by binary fission. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Choose the correct order of events in the Nitrogen Cycle.

A) Nitrogen in the air -> Animals get nitrogen from plants -> Bacteria fix nitrogen -> Animals die and decompose

B) Animals die and decompose -> Animals get nitrogen from plants -> Nitrogen in the air -> Bacteria fix nitrogen

C) Bacteria fix nitrogen -> Nitrogen in the air -> Animals get nitrogen from plants -> Animals die and decompose

D) Nitrogen in the air -> Bacteria fix nitrogen -> Animals get nitrogen from plants -> Animals die and decompose
questions.corrige_markdown: The cycle starts with atmospheric nitrogen, which bacteria (nitrogen-fixing bacteria) convert into nitrates in the soil. Plants absorb the nitrates and make proteins, animals obtain nitrogen by eating plants, and when organisms die, decomposers return nitrogen compounds to the soil. Only D follows this order. In A the fixation step comes after animals have already used nitrogen, in B the sequence starts with death and decay, and in C bacteria fix nitrogen before it is 'in the air'. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Nitrogen in the air, animals get nitrogen from plants, bacteria fix nitrogen, animals die and decompose.
Animals die and decompose, animals get nitrogen from plants, nitrogen in the air, bacteria fix nitrogen.
Bacteria fix nitrogen, nitrogen in the air, animals get nitrogen from plants, animals die and decompose.
Nitrogen in the air, bacteria fix nitrogen, animals get nitrogen from plants, animals die and decompose.

questions.enonce_markdown: A solution obtained from crushed germinating bean seeds was tested with Millon's reagent and a red colour was observed. This indicates the presence of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Millon's reagent gives a brick-red (red) colour with proteins (it reacts with the amino acid tyrosine). Starch is tested with iodine solution (blue-black), reducing sugar with Benedict's solution (brick-red precipitate on heating) and lipids with the ethanol emulsion test or the grease-spot test. Do not confuse Millon's red with Benedict's brick-red. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which part of the alimentary canal produces bile?
questions.corrige_markdown: Bile is made by the liver. It is stored in the gall bladder and released into the duodenum, but the gall bladder does not produce it. The stomach produces gastric juice. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which layer of the skin produces melanin?
questions.corrige_markdown: Melanin, the dark pigment that protects against ultraviolet light, is made by cells in the Malpighian (germinative) layer at the base of the epidermis. The cornified layer is the dead outer layer, the granular layer lies above the Malpighian layer, and the subcutaneous layer is fat tissue below the dermis. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What structure protects the lizard's body from mechanical injury?
questions.corrige_markdown: The body of a lizard is covered with horny, waterproof scales that protect it from mechanical injury and from water loss. The tail is used for balance and fat storage (and can be shed), and the claws are for gripping. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is that of a plant cell.

![fig-1](gce-ol-biology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Which of the numbered structures contain chlorophyll?
questions.corrige_markdown: Chlorophyll is found in chloroplasts. In the diagram, structure 3 is the oval body with internal cross-hatching that represents the grana of a chloroplast (the unlabelled oval at the bottom of the cell is drawn the same way). Structure 1 is the dark, solid body pushed to the edge of the cell by the large vacuole: it is the nucleus. Structure 2 is the boundary of the large central vacuole and 4 is the cytoplasm, neither of which contains chlorophyll. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The part of the eye responsible for image formation is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Light is refracted by the cornea and lens, but the image is actually formed on the retina, the light-sensitive layer that contains the rods and cones. The pupil only controls how much light enters and the choroid contains blood vessels and pigment. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is a presentation of the water cycle.

![fig-2](gce-ol-biology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

Which of the following processes is represented by 3?
questions.corrige_markdown: Arrow 3 goes from the water bodies to the plants: plants take up water from the soil and water bodies through their roots, which is absorption. Arrow 1 (clouds to water bodies) is precipitation, arrow 2 (plants to water vapour in the atmosphere) is transpiration and arrow 4 (water bodies to the atmosphere) is evaporation. Guttation is the loss of liquid water from leaf margins and is not shown. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which structure prevents the back flow of blood into the right atrium?
questions.corrige_markdown: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle and closes when the ventricle contracts, so blood cannot flow back into the right atrium. The bicuspid (mitral) valve does the same job on the left side, and the semi-lunar valves are at the exits of the ventricles. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: This structure is responsible for forward movement in the bony fish.
questions.corrige_markdown: The tail (caudal) fin, driven by the side-to-side contraction of the body muscles, pushes against the water and propels the fish forward. The pectoral and pelvic fins are used for steering, braking and balance, and the dorsal fin prevents rolling. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which part of the female reproductive system is the site for implantation of the embryo?
questions.corrige_markdown: The embryo reaches the uterus and embeds in its thick, blood-rich lining (endometrium): this is implantation. Fertilisation takes place in the oviduct; the vagina receives the sperms and the cervix is the opening of the uterus. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below shows the position of endocrine glands.

![fig-3](gce-ol-biology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

Which of the numbered structure secretes a hormone that controls ovulation in females?

*Options as printed:* A) 1. B) 4. C) 2. D) 5.
questions.corrige_markdown: The question is left open because the key cannot be fixed with certainty from the diagram. Ovulation is controlled by the pituitary gland, which secretes FSH (ripening of the follicle) and LH (release of the egg). In the diagram two small structures, 1 and 2, are drawn side by side inside the head and are not distinguishable (pituitary gland and a neighbouring structure such as the hypothalamus or pineal gland); 3 is the thyroid gland, X the pancreas, 4 the ovary (one of a symmetrical pair in the lower abdomen) and 5 a structure at the midline. The ovary (4) also secretes oestrogen, which triggers the LH surge and so also influences ovulation. Most likely intended answer: the pituitary gland, option A (1), but 2 and 4 are also defensible, so no letter is designated.

questions.enonce_markdown: It reduces friction during the movement of the elbow joint:
questions.corrige_markdown: Smooth cartilage covers the ends of the bones in a synovial joint, and together with synovial fluid it reduces friction. Ligaments join bone to bone, tendons join muscle to bone and the humerus is a bone. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The structure of a nerve cell that conducts impulses away from the cell body:
questions.corrige_markdown: The axon is the long fibre that carries impulses away from the cell body. The dendron and the dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body, and the myelin sheath is the fatty insulation around the axon (it speeds up conduction but does not conduct). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The blood vessel most likely to contain food nutrients a few hours after eating a heavy meal;
questions.corrige_markdown: Digested food (glucose, amino acids) is absorbed into the capillaries of the villi and carried to the liver by the hepatic portal vein, so this vessel has the highest nutrient content after a meal. The hepatic artery brings oxygenated blood to the liver, the renal vein carries blood from the kidney and the aorta carries blood that has already passed through the liver and been mixed. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The structure in Spirogyra that enables it to carry out autotrophic nutrition:
questions.corrige_markdown: Spirogyra makes its own food by photosynthesis, using the spiral chloroplast that contains chlorophyll. The pyrenoids are only starch-forming centres on the chloroplast, the mucilage is a slimy covering and the cytoplasmic strands hold the nucleus in the centre of the cell. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following structure is involved in gaseous exchange in the lungs?
questions.corrige_markdown: Gaseous exchange takes place in the alveoli: they have thin, moist walls and a rich blood supply, so oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out. The trachea, bronchi and bronchioles only conduct air. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
From the food chain below, what trophic level is occupied by the goat?

Sun -> maize -> goat -> lion
questions.corrige_markdown: Maize is the producer (first trophic level). The goat feeds directly on the producer, so it is a primary consumer (herbivore, second trophic level). The lion eating the goat is the secondary consumer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. B) If 1 and 2 only are correct. C) If 2 and 3 only are correct. D) If 1 only is correct.

In a food chain:

1. Producers are autotrophic organisms.
2. Each organism has many food sources.
3. Producers release carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.
questions.corrige_markdown: 1 is true: producers (green plants) make their own food. 2 is false: in a food chain each organism is shown feeding on one other organism (many food sources are shown in a food web). 3 is false: during photosynthesis producers take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen; they release carbon dioxide only in respiration. Only 1 is correct. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. B) If 1 and 2 only are correct. C) If 2 and 3 only are correct. D) If 1 only is correct.

During the bending movement of the arm:

1. The biceps muscles contract.
2. The triceps muscles relax.
3. The ulna and radius straighten.
questions.corrige_markdown: To bend (flex) the arm the biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes (antagonistic pair). Statement 3 is false: the ulna and radius are pulled towards the humerus and the arm bends, it is straightening that occurs when the triceps contracts. Only 1 and 2 are correct. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. B) If 1 and 2 only are correct. C) If 2 and 3 only are correct. D) If 1 only is correct.

Myopia (short sightedness):

1. Occurs as a result of the eyeball being large.
2. Near objects are seen clearly.
3. Is corrected with the use of concave lenses.
questions.corrige_markdown: Myopia is caused by an eyeball that is too long (large) or a lens that is too strong, so the image of distant objects forms in front of the retina. Near objects can be focused on the retina and are seen clearly, while distant objects are blurred. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays before they enter the eye and corrects the defect. All three statements are correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. B) If 1 and 2 only are correct. C) If 2 and 3 only are correct. D) If 1 only is correct.

In temperature control during overheating:

1. Sweating is inhibited.
2. Vasodilation occurs.
3. The hair erector muscles relax.
questions.corrige_markdown: When the body is too hot, sweating increases (so statement 1 is false), the arterioles in the skin widen (vasodilation) so more blood flows near the surface and loses heat, and the hair erector muscles relax so the hairs lie flat and trap less air. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose:* A) If 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. B) If 1 and 2 only are correct. C) If 2 and 3 only are correct. D) If 1 only is correct.

Birds fly easily because:

1. They have wings.
2. They have hollow bones.
3. They have streamline bodies.
questions.corrige_markdown: Wings give lift, hollow (air-filled) bones make the body light and a streamlined body reduces air resistance. All three are adaptations for flight. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose A, B, C or D as in the table of the paper:* A) first true, second true, 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B) first true, second true, 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C) first true, second false; D) first false, second true.

**First statement:** During anaerobic respiration glucose is partially broken down.

**Second statement:** Anaerobic respiration occurs in the cytoplasm.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: in anaerobic respiration glucose is broken down only to ethanol and carbon dioxide (in yeast) or to lactic acid (in muscle), so only part of its energy is released, and the process takes place in the cytoplasm. The question is left open because the choice between A and B is a matter of judgement. The partial breakdown is mainly explained by the absence of oxygen: the further steps need oxygen and the mitochondria, which argues for B (not a correct explanation). On the other hand, because anaerobic respiration is restricted to the cytoplasm and does not reach the mitochondria, the breakdown stays incomplete, which argues for A. No letter is designated.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose A, B, C or D:* A) both statements true and the 2nd is a correct explanation of the first; B) both true and the 2nd is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C) first true, second false; D) first false, second true.

**First statement:** Arteries have small lumen and thick elastic walls.

**Second statement:** Arteries carry blood away from the heart.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Arteries carry blood away from the heart at high pressure, and this is why they have thick, elastic, muscular walls and a narrow lumen: the walls must withstand and smooth out the pressure surges from the heart. The second statement therefore explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: First statement true, second statement true, and the second statement is a correct explanation of the first.
First statement true, second statement true, and the second statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
First statement true, second statement false.
First statement false, second statement true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose A, B, C or D:* A) both statements true and the 2nd is a correct explanation of the first; B) both true and the 2nd is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C) first true, second false; D) first false, second true.

**First statement:** Fresh water Amoeba possesses contractile vacuole.

**Second statement:** The cytoplasm of fresh water Amoeba is more concentrated than the surrounding water.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Because the cytoplasm is more concentrated than the surrounding fresh water, water enters the cell by osmosis all the time. The contractile vacuole removes this excess water, so the second statement explains why the contractile vacuole is needed. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: First statement true, second statement true, and the second statement is a correct explanation of the first.
First statement true, second statement true, and the second statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
First statement true, second statement false.
First statement false, second statement true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose A, B, C or D as in the table of the paper:* A) first true, second true, 2nd statement is a correct explanation of the first; B) first true, second true, 2nd statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C) first true, second false; D) first false, second true.

**First statement:** Acid rain results when Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide are released into the atmosphere.

**Second statement:** Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide in the atmosphere originate from the burning of fuel.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true: sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide dissolve in rain water to form sulphurous, sulphuric and nitric acids, and these gases come mainly from the burning of fossil fuels (and from volcanoes and vehicle engines). The question is left open because the choice between A and B is a matter of judgement: the second statement tells where the gases come from (the origin of the pollutants), not why they cause acid rain, which argues for B; but it gives the cause of their presence in the atmosphere, which argues for A. No letter is designated.

questions.enonce_markdown:
*Choose A, B, C or D:* A) both statements true and the 2nd is a correct explanation of the first; B) both true and the 2nd is NOT a correct explanation of the first; C) first true, second false; D) first false, second true.

**First statement:** The body of most mammals is covered with fur or hair.

**Second statement:** Fur or hair assist in the control of body temperature.
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Fur or hair traps a layer of air next to the skin, which insulates the body, and the hair erector muscles adjust its thickness (raised when cold, flat when hot). This temperature control is the reason mammals have a hair covering, so the second statement explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: First statement true, second statement true, and the second statement is a correct explanation of the first.
First statement true, second statement true, and the second statement is NOT a correct explanation of the first.
First statement true, second statement false.
First statement false, second statement true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* The process that releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere:
questions.corrige_markdown: Respiration breaks down food and releases carbon dioxide (and water) that passes into the atmosphere. Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air, chemosynthesis is the making of food from inorganic compounds without light, and precipitation is rain, snow or hail. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* Controls balance and posture:
questions.corrige_markdown: The cerebellum coordinates muscular activity and controls balance and posture. The cerebrum is for thinking, memory and voluntary action, the hypothalamus controls body temperature and water balance, and the medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions such as breathing and heartbeat. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* A pair of non-identical genes for the same characteristics:
questions.corrige_markdown: A pair of non-identical alleles (for example Aa) for one characteristic is heterozygous. Homozygous means the two alleles are identical (AA or aa), the genotype is the genetic make-up and the phenotype is the observable appearance. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* An association between two organisms in which both benefit.
questions.corrige_markdown: In mutualism both partners benefit (for example nitrogen-fixing bacteria in root nodules of legumes). In parasitism only the parasite benefits, saprophytes feed on dead organic matter and in predation the predator benefits at the expense of the prey. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* A natural self-sustaining unit.
questions.corrige_markdown: An ecosystem is a natural unit made of a community of living organisms and their physical environment, interacting and recycling materials. Ecology is the study of such relationships, the environment is the surroundings and the atmosphere is the layer of gases around the Earth. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* Produced during fright.
questions.corrige_markdown: Adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands, prepares the body for fright, fight or flight (faster heartbeat, more glucose in the blood). Insulin and glucagon regulate blood sugar and thyroxine controls the metabolic rate. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* Causes malaria.
questions.corrige_markdown: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan parasite. The female anopheles mosquito is only the vector that carries it from person to person (it does not cause the disease itself), culex mosquitoes transmit other diseases such as filariasis, and the male anopheles does not bite. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* Its deficiency will lead to anaemia.
questions.corrige_markdown: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin, so lack of iron causes anaemia. Lack of calcium and phosphorus affects bones and teeth (rickets) and lack of iodine causes goitre. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* Used for tearing of flesh.
questions.corrige_markdown: The pointed canines tear flesh. The incisors cut, and the premolars and molars crush and grind food. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Select the heading which is closely related to the description that follows.

*Description:* Is an air pollutant.
questions.corrige_markdown: Lead particles from the exhaust of vehicles that use leaded petrol are a classic air pollutant. Nitrogen gas (78 % of air) and oxygen (21 %) are normal constituents of air, not pollutants, and mercury is mostly known as a water and soil pollutant. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When red blood corpuscles were mounted in distilled water for 20 minutes, only cell fragments remained in solution. This is due to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Distilled water is more dilute than the cytoplasm of the red blood cell, so water enters the cell by osmosis; an animal cell has no cell wall, so it swells and bursts (haemolysis), leaving only fragments. Wilting, turgidity and plasmolysis describe plant cells (plasmolysis is loss of water from a cell in a concentrated solution). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In many perennial plants, soluble products of photosynthesis are transported from the leaves to underground storage organs. This is possible through:
questions.corrige_markdown: Translocation is the movement of soluble organic substances (sucrose, amino acids) in the phloem from the leaves to storage organs and growing regions. Root pressure and the transpiration stream move water and mineral salts upwards in the xylem. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two sets of apparatus were used to investigate the process of photosynthesis. Before the set ups were exposed to sunlight, both plants were kept in the dark for 48 hours. What colour change is observed when iodine is used to test for starch in the leaves?

*Options as printed:* A) Orange. B) Dark blue. C) Deep red. D) Dark green.
questions.corrige_markdown: The question is left open because the key depends on when the test is carried out, which the question does not say. Keeping the plants in the dark for 48 hours destarches them. If the leaves are tested before the exposure to sunlight, they contain no starch and the iodine solution stays orange-brown (option A, no colour change). If the leaves are tested after exposure, a leaf that has photosynthesised in light with all the necessary conditions contains starch and iodine turns blue-black (option B, 'dark blue'); the wording 'colour change' suggests B, which is probably the intended answer. Deep red and dark green are never produced by the iodine test for starch. No letter is designated.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In an investigation of the effects of external factors on body temperature of various animals, the following results were shown graphically.

![fig-4](gce-ol-biology-2026-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

From the graph above, the rat is described as:
questions.corrige_markdown: The body temperature of the rat is a horizontal line at about 37 degrees Celsius whatever the external temperature: it keeps a constant body temperature, so it is homoiothermic (warm-blooded). The toad's body temperature rises with the external temperature, so the toad is ectothermic and poikilothermic (options B and D describe the toad, not the rat). Exothermic is a chemical term for a reaction that gives out heat. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The table below shows the composition of four different food.

| Food | Carbohydrates (g) | Fat (g) | Proteins (g) | Iron (mg) | Calcium (mg) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H | 4.8 | 3.5 | 2.7 | 0.01 | 10.5 |
| P | 4.0 | 5.2 | 2.5 | 1.5 | 0.9 |
| S | 5.0 | 0.2 | 1.6 | 0.25 | 2.8 |
| R | 8.0 | 0.1 | 2.4 | 0.05 | 0.7 |

Which food will best prevent anaemia?
questions.corrige_markdown: Anaemia is a lack of haemoglobin, usually due to iron deficiency, so the best food is the one richest in iron. Iron content: P = 1.5 mg, S = 0.25 mg, R = 0.05 mg, H = 0.01 mg. Food P has by far the most iron. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In rabbits, albinism (white fur and pink eyes) represented by 'a' is recessive to black fur colour and black eyes represented by 'A'. An albino male is crossed with a pure breeding black female. What is the probability of producing a normal $F_2$ offspring?
questions.corrige_markdown: Albino male = aa; pure-breeding black female = AA. All F1 offspring are Aa (black). The F2 is obtained by crossing the F1 among themselves: Aa x Aa gives AA : Aa : Aa : aa, that is 3 normal (black) to 1 albino, so the probability of a normal F2 offspring is 3/4. The value 1 (option D) is the probability of a normal F1 offspring, the common trap if the generation is misread. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A fish suffocates and dies if taken out of water. This is due to the fact that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Out of water the gill filaments collapse and stick together, so the surface area for gaseous exchange is greatly reduced and not enough oxygen can be absorbed. Option C is false: air contains much more oxygen than water (about 21 % against a very small amount dissolved in water), and the carbon dioxide in air is very small. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: There is little oxygen in the air than water.
There is much carbon dioxide in the air than in water.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The graph below shows the effect of temperature on the rate of photosynthesis.

What is the significance of point X on the graph?
questions.corrige_markdown: Point X is the peak of the curve: the rate rises with temperature up to X (the optimum temperature of the enzymes), and beyond X it falls because the enzymes are denatured. X is therefore the maximum rate of photosynthesis. **Answer: B.**

Why does the population of predators drop by the fifth year?
questions.corrige_markdown: The number of prey falls steadily from 500 to 30 over the five years, because the predators eat them. By year 4 and 5 there is not enough prey to feed the predators, so many starve and the predator population drops (from 10 in year 3 to 3 in year 5).
